details.description: Claude Opus 5.5 is Anthropic's current Opus-tier model, released September 22, 2026 as the first model in a new '5.5' family and the successor to Claude Opus 5. Anthropic reports it performs at the level of its higher Claude Fable 5.1 tier on most work while costing 40% less to run than Opus 5 and generating output more than 30% faster. It has a 1-million-token context window, vision input, and adaptive thinking that is always on and cannot be disabled, and it is built for long-running agentic coding, computer use and knowledge work.
advantages: Scores 66.4% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, an agentic coding and terminal-use benchmark (Anthropic launch post).
Scores 81.8% (partial-credit) on the OSWorld 2.0 computer-use benchmark (Anthropic launch post).
Scores 89.0% (with tools) on Chartography, a visual chart-recognition benchmark (Anthropic launch post).
Scores 67.7% (with tools) on Humanity's Last Exam, a multidisciplinary reasoning evaluation (Anthropic launch post).
Anthropic reports it is the strongest-performing model to date on its automated behavioral safety audit (Anthropic launch post).
One tester reported completing a 680,000-line code migration in under a day (Anthropic launch post).
disadvantages: Adaptive thinking is always on and cannot be disabled, a breaking behavior change from Claude Opus 5 (Anthropic model reference).
Anthropic states that at this capability level, 'benchmark margins have become a less reliable guide to real-world differences' (Anthropic launch post).
Reliable knowledge cutoff of June 2026 (Anthropic model reference).
use_cases: Long-running agentic coding and large-scale code migrations
Enterprise knowledge work, including financial analysis and research
Delegating work to subagents with self-verification

sources.title: Claude Opus 5.5: Anthropic's Cheaper, Faster New Flagship

notes: Catalog has no deprecation_date fact for this model; Anthropic's model-deprecations table gives a tentative retirement 'Not sooner than September 22, 2027,' consistent with it being the current Opus model ('Latest' status on platform.claude.com). Catalog's 1M max input / 128K max output tokens and image+text-in/text-out modality match platform.claude.com's specs table exactly. Benchmark percentages were confirmed verbatim in Anthropic's own launch-post prose (re-fetched twice, including its footnotes section) and cross-checked against DataCamp's independent write-up of the same figures, which matched exactly.
